ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Flow-matching action head for a decision-pretrained transformer
PROPOSAL: We pretrain a decision-pretrained transformer on a pooled offline corpus from eight continuous-control families, replacing the discrete action readout through a conditional flow-matching head that samples actions natively from the transformer output given the query state and the in-context transitions. The 400000 trajectories carry expert action labels. Training uses a 60M-parameter backbone and a context of 256 transitions. We evaluate normalized return on 24 unseen tasks and on parametric variations of training environments, once with an empty context filled by the agent's own interaction over 20 episodes and once with five expert demonstrations.
CONTROLS: Three other heads trained on the same corpus and backbone: a diagonal Gaussian, a mixture of Gaussians with eight components and a deterministic regression. Algorithm Distillation trained on the same data gives the in-context reference, and three seeds give the spread.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: The flow-matching head should beat the Gaussian head on multi-modal tasks and keep posterior-sampling behaviour as the context grows. Gains may be small on tasks with a single optimal action.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Action head comparison for a decision-pretrained transformer in continuous control
PROPOSAL: We pretrain a decision-pretrained transformer on a pooled offline corpus from eight continuous-control families, comparing action heads: diagonal Gaussian, mixtures with four to sixteen components, flow matching, diffusion with ten to fifty denoising steps, and discretized heads with sixty-four to 256 bins per dimension. Each head is trained with transformers of 30M to 120M parameters on corpora of 100000 to 400000 trajectories, with contexts of 128 to 512 transitions. Heads are compared at matched optimizer settings and matched training steps. We evaluate normalized return on twenty-four unseen tasks and on parametric variations, with empty and demonstration-filled contexts.
CONTROLS: Algorithm Distillation and a deterministic regression head trained on the same corpora. Heads are compared at matched parameter counts, and three seeds give the spread for each configuration.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Flow and diffusion heads should lead on multi-modal tasks, with differences among denoising step counts shrinking beyond 25 steps. Mixture heads may be competitive on simple locomotion.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-domain tokenizers for heterogeneous observation and action spaces in in-context reinforcement learning
PROPOSAL: We pretrain a decision-pretrained transformer on offline data from eight families whose observation dimensions range from 11 to 376 and whose action dimensions range from 1 to 38. Each domain receives its own linear tokenizer for states, actions and rewards, mapped into a shared 512-dimensional space, followed by a shared 150M-parameter transformer and a flow-matching action head using a per-domain output projection. The corpus holds 2 million trajectories. We evaluate normalized return on unseen tasks from each family, measuring adaptation over 30 episodes of self-collected context.
CONTROLS: A single fixed-dimension interface with zero-filling of missing coordinates, a shared tokenizer with domain embeddings, and per-domain single-task transformers as an upper reference. Three seeds give the spread, and Algorithm Distillation serves as the in-context baseline.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Per-domain tokenizers should beat zero-filling on families with the most different dimensions and approach single-task transformers. Positive transfer between families may be weak.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Tokenization schemes for heterogeneous spaces in in-context reinforcement learning
PROPOSAL: We pretrain a decision-pretrained transformer on offline data from eight families whose observation dimensions range from eleven to 376 and whose action dimensions range from 1 to 38, comparing per-domain linear tokenizers, per-coordinate tokenizers, a shared tokenizer with domain embeddings, zero-filled fixed interfaces and learned set encoders, with shared widths of 256, 512 and 1024 and transformers of 50M, 150M and 400M parameters. Corpora hold 1, two and four million trajectories. We evaluate normalized return on unseen tasks from each family, measuring adaptation over thirty episodes of self-collected context.
CONTROLS: Per-domain single-task transformers as an upper reference, Algorithm Distillation as the in-context baseline, and a flow-matching head and a Gaussian head for each scheme. Five seeds give the spread for each configuration.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Per-domain tokenizers should beat zero-filling where dimensions differ most. Per-coordinate schemes may not pay off at the smallest scale.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Context composition for a decision-pretrained transformer in continuous control
PROPOSAL: We train a decision-pretrained transformer whose in-context dataset is built from three sources of transitions: random exploration, trajectories of a partially trained learner and trajectories of an expert, mixed at fixed ratios during pretraining, plus a flow-matching head and a 100M-parameter backbone on eight domains. At test time we fill the context with the agent's own interaction history and measure normalized return after 5, 20 and 50 episodes on 24 unseen tasks. We test whether the model keeps its behaviour when the context is empty at the start.
CONTROLS: Pretraining only on expert contexts, only on exploratory contexts and on a fixed uniform mixture, plus a model that sees no context. Algorithm Distillation provides the in-context baseline, and three seeds give the spread.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Mixed contexts should give the best adaptation from an empty start. Expert-only contexts may fail when test tasks differ in dynamics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Context composition and length study for a decision-pretrained transformer in continuous control
PROPOSAL: We train a decision-pretrained transformer whose in-context dataset is built from random exploration, trajectories of partially trained learners at five stages and trajectories of an expert, mixed at 12 ratios during pretraining, with context lengths from sixty-four to 1024 transitions, flow-matching and Gaussian heads, and transformers of 30M to 300M parameters on eight domains. At test time we fill the context with the agent's own history and measure normalized return after five to 100 episodes on 24 unseen tasks and on parametric variations.
CONTROLS: Pretraining only on expert contexts, only on exploratory contexts, a fixed uniform mixture, and a model with no context. Algorithm Distillation provides the in-context baseline, and three seeds give the spread for each setting.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Mixed contexts should give the best adaptation, with longer contexts helping up to a point. Expert-only contexts may fail when dynamics change.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Posterior-sampling check for a continuous-action in-context learner
PROPOSAL: We test whether a pretrained flow-matching decision-pretrained transformer behaves like a posterior sampler over optimal actions. On families of tasks with a known posterior, namely contextual bandits with 2-dimensional actions and linear-quadratic control with varied gravity, we compare the distribution of sampled actions to the exact posterior using the Wasserstein distance as the context grows from 0 to 128 transitions. We then measure normalized return on MuJoCo locomotion tasks when actions are sampled and when the mean action is used.
CONTROLS: Two other heads with the same backbone, a Gaussian and a deterministic one, and the exact posterior from conjugate updates as the reference. Three seeds give the spread, and the context order is shuffled to test permutation sensitivity.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: The flow-matching head should track the exact posterior with a distance that falls as context grows. Sampling may lose to the mean action on tasks with narrow optima.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Posterior-sampling checks over many task families for a continuous-action in-context learner
PROPOSAL: We test whether pretrained decision-pretrained transformers with flow-matching, diffusion, Gaussian and mixture heads behave like posterior samplers. On contextual bandits with 1, 2 and four-dimensional actions and on linear-quadratic control with five gravity values and four mass values, we compare the distribution of sampled actions to the exact posterior with Wasserstein and energy distances as the context grows from 0 to 512 transitions. We then measure normalized return on six MuJoCo locomotion tasks when actions are sampled and when the mean action is used.
CONTROLS: A deterministic head with the same backbone, and the exact posterior from conjugate updates as the reference. Five seeds give the spread, context order is shuffled at ten levels, and context lengths are varied at each setting.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Flow and diffusion heads should track the exact posterior with a distance that falls as context grows. Sampling may lose to the mean action on narrow optima.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model and data scaling laws for a decision-pretrained transformer
PROPOSAL: We train decision-pretrained transformers with 25M, 100M and 400M parameters on corpora of 0.5, 2 and eight million trajectories drawn from eight continuous-control families, all using a flow-matching head and a context of 256 transitions. For each model and corpus size we measure normalized return on 24 unseen tasks, on parametric variations of training environments, and under demonstration prompting with five expert trajectories. We fit a power law to the adaptation gap to the per-task experts, and read the exponent for model size and for data size.
CONTROLS: A matched Algorithm Distillation model at each size, a single-task transformer for each family, and one retrained model with a different seed at the middle size to show training variance.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: The gap to experts should shrink with both axes, with data mattering more than parameters for unseen tasks. Gains may saturate at the largest data size if families overlap.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model and data scaling grid for a decision-pretrained transformer in continuous control
PROPOSAL: We train decision-pretrained transformers over a ladder of seven sizes from 10M to 800M parameters on corpora over a ladder of seven sizes from 0.25 to 16 million trajectories drawn from eight continuous-control families, with flow-matching, diffusion and Gaussian heads and contexts of 128 to 512 transitions. For each model and corpus we measure normalized return on twenty-four unseen tasks, on parametric variations of training environments, and under demonstration prompting with 1 to 20 expert trajectories. We fit power laws to the adaptation gap for each head.
CONTROLS: A matched Algorithm Distillation model at each size, a single-task transformer for each family, and retrained models with five seeds at four sizes to show training variance.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: The gap to experts should shrink along both axes, with data mattering more than parameters. Gains may saturate at the highest data sizes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Self-corrective adaptation of a continuous-action in-context learner in building control
PROPOSAL: We deploy a pretrained flow-matching decision-pretrained transformer with no demonstrations on unseen HVAC and building energy tasks with shifted weather and occupancy, letting the context fill with its own interaction. Over 50 episodes we track comfort violation and energy use, and we test a rule that restricts the context to the most recent 128 transitions. We compare adaptation curves on 12 unseen building tasks and on parametric variations of four training buildings, with 3 seeds for the rollouts.
CONTROLS: Soft actor-critic trained from scratch on each task, Algorithm Distillation with the same context, the same transformer with a frozen empty context, and a retrieval baseline with expert demonstrations.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The learner should reduce comfort violation within 20 episodes faster than training from scratch. Early episodes may be unsafe if the context starts empty.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Self-corrective adaptation of continuous-action in-context learners in many control domains
PROPOSAL: We deploy pretrained decision-pretrained transformers with flow-matching, diffusion and Gaussian heads with no demonstrations on unseen HVAC, building energy, driving, industrial process and humanoid tasks with shifted dynamics, letting the context fill with their own interaction. Over 100 episodes we track return, constraint violation and energy use, and test context windows of 64, 128, 256 and 512 transitions. We compare adaptation curves on forty unseen tasks and on parametric variations of twelve training environments, with five seeds for the rollouts and a fixed evaluation schedule.
CONTROLS: Soft actor-critic from scratch on each task, Algorithm Distillation with the same context, the same transformers with a frozen empty context, and a retrieval baseline with expert demonstrations.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The learner should reduce violations within 20 episodes faster than training from scratch. Early episodes may be unsafe while the context is empty.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Demonstration prompting of a continuous-action in-context learner on unseen tasks
PROPOSAL: We pretrain a flow-matching decision-pretrained transformer using a 200M-parameter backbone on four million trajectories from eight families, then prompt it with 1, five or 20 expert demonstrations on 30 unseen tasks of robot manipulation, humanoid control and PDE control, without gradient updates. We measure normalized return against the number of demonstrations and against the distance of the test task from the training tasks, defined by an embedding of environment parameters, and we measure sensitivity to demonstration quality using 3 levels of expert strength.
CONTROLS: Behaviour cloning fine-tuned on the same demonstrations, a retrieval-augmented transformer, Algorithm Distillation with the same prompt, and a generalist agent from prior work evaluated on the same tasks. Three seeds give the spread.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Return should rise with the number of demonstrations and fall with distance from training tasks, beating fine-tuned cloning at 1 demonstration. Gains over retrieval may vanish for tasks far from the corpus.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Demonstration prompting of continuous-action in-context learners over model sizes and domains
PROPOSAL: We pretrain flow-matching and diffusion decision-pretrained transformers with 50M, 200M and 600M parameters on 1, four and eight million trajectories from eight families, then prompt them with 1, 2, 5, ten and twenty expert demonstrations on eighty unseen tasks of robot manipulation, humanoid control, driving, process control and PDE control, without gradient updates. We measure normalized return against the number of demonstrations and the distance from training tasks, and sensitivity to demonstration quality using five levels of expert strength and three prompt orderings.
CONTROLS: Behaviour cloning fine-tuned on the same demonstrations, a retrieval-augmented transformer, Algorithm Distillation with the same prompt, and a generalist agent from prior work evaluated on the same tasks. Five seeds give the spread for each model.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Return should rise with the number of demonstrations and fall with distance from training tasks. Bigger models may help only on far tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pilot of action-head choices on two control families
PROPOSAL: We pretrain a small decision-pretrained transformer with 20M parameters on offline data from robot locomotion and PDE control, 100000 trajectories each, with flow-matching and Gaussian action heads and a context of 128 transitions. We evaluate normalized return on six unseen tasks of each family after 10 episodes of self-collected context, and measure the negative log-likelihood of held-out expert actions to see whether multi-modality appears in the data at all. The pilot decides whether the full corpus is worth building.
CONTROLS: Two other heads, deterministic and Gaussian, a model with empty context, and per-task experts as the ceiling. Two seeds show whether the head ranking is stable.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: The flow head should lower negative log-likelihood on locomotion and show a smaller gain on PDE control. The ranking may flip between seeds at this size.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Study of action-head choices on all eight control families with small model sizes
PROPOSAL: We pretrain decision-pretrained transformers with 10M to 50M parameters on offline data from all eight control families, 100000 to 400000 trajectories each, with flow-matching, diffusion, mixture and Gaussian action heads and contexts of sixty-four to 256 transitions. We evaluate normalized return on six unseen tasks of each family after ten and fifty episodes of self-collected context, and measure the negative log-likelihood of held-out expert actions for each head and family.
CONTROLS: A deterministic head, a model with empty context, and per-task experts as the ceiling. Five seeds show whether the head ranking is stable, and each setting is rerun with a second corpus draw.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Flow and diffusion heads should lower negative log-likelihood on locomotion and gain less on PDE control. Rankings may flip between seeds at the smallest size.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leave-one-family-out generalization of an in-context reinforcement learner
PROPOSAL: We pretrain a flow-matching decision-pretrained transformer on 7 of eight control families and test on the held-out family, repeating the procedure with each family left out in turn. The backbone has 100M parameters and the corpus holds 3 million trajectories over the 7 training families. We measure normalized return on unseen tasks of the held-out family with an empty context, with the agent's own history over 30 episodes and with five expert demonstrations, and we relate the result to the similarity between families measured by dynamics embeddings.
CONTROLS: A model trained on all eight families, a single-task transformer on the held-out family, and Algorithm Distillation under the same leave-one-out protocol. Three seeds give the spread.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Held-out return should fall with dynamics distance, and demonstrations should shrink the gap more than self-collected context. Closely related families may show almost no gap.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leave-out generalization of in-context reinforcement learners over many family subsets
PROPOSAL: We pretrain flow-matching and Gaussian-head decision-pretrained transformers on subsets of 2, 4, six and seven of eight control families, drawn in all twenty-eight pairs, twenty quadruples, eight sextuples and each leave-one-out split, and test on the held-out families. Backbones have 50M, 100M and 300M parameters and corpora hold 1 to three million trajectories. We measure normalized return with an empty context, with the agent's own history over thirty episodes and with 1, five and twenty expert demonstrations, and relate it to family similarity measured by dynamics embeddings.
CONTROLS: A model trained on all eight families, single-task transformers on the held-out families, and Algorithm Distillation under the same splits. Three seeds give the spread for each subset.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Held-out return should fall with dynamics distance and with fewer training families. Demonstrations should shrink the gap more than self-collected context. The effect should be clearest for the most distant held-out families.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expert-label quality for the optimal-action target of a decision-pretrained transformer
PROPOSAL: The decision-pretrained objective needs the optimal action for each query state, but offline continuous-control corpora only hold the actions of imperfect experts. We build labels for 3 locomotion tasks from soft actor-critic policies trained to 3 levels of return, and from a one-step improvement of the best policy through a learned critic. We pretrain 20M-parameter transformers with a Gaussian head on each label set and measure normalized return on six unseen task variations after 20 episodes of self-collected context.
CONTROLS: Labels from the behaviour policy itself, labels from the best policy without improvement, and a label set mixing all levels. Two seeds show whether the effect exceeds training noise. Each label set is built once and shared by all runs.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Improved labels should raise return and shorten adaptation compared with raw expert actions. The critic may add bias that cancels the gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expert-label sources for the optimal-action target of a decision-pretrained transformer on many tasks
PROPOSAL: Offline continuous-control corpora hold the actions of imperfect experts, yet the decision-pretrained objective asks for the optimal action at each query state. For 16 tasks we derive labels from soft actor-critic and proximal policy optimization policies of five quality grades, from critic-guided improvement steps with 1 to ten gradient iterations. Transformers of 20M and 60M parameters with Gaussian and flow-matching heads are pretrained on each label set, and we measure normalized return on twenty-four unseen task variations after 20 episodes of self-collected context.
CONTROLS: Labels from the behaviour policy itself, labels from the best policy without improvement, and label sets mixing all levels. Five seeds show whether the effect exceeds training noise for each setting.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Improved labels should raise return and shorten adaptation compared with raw expert actions. The critic may add bias that cancels the gain on tasks with sparse rewards.
